prompts.content:
### ⚖️ MANDATORY 50/50 MEDIA SPLIT (50% VIDEO / 50% IMAGE)
Every episode must maintain an exact 50/50 split between static image scenes and moving video scenes across the entire duration.
Follow an alternating rhythm throughout the timeline (Scene 1 MUST always be a video to hook the user):
- Odd scenes (Scene 1, Scene 3, Scene 5, ...): MOTION VIDEO CLIP (<video_prompt[N]>)
- Even scenes (Scene 2, Scene 4, Scene 6, ...): STATIC IMAGE (<image_prompt[N]>)
Ensure exactly 50% of the scenes are designated as image assets and 50% as video assets.

STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image/video prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic, Source Material, and Input/Canon Packet. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently (do not output your notes unless the template asks for a packet) and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened (or, for fiction: the locked rule, canon, and inputs supplied), who is involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, popular myth, or unestablished canon.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume/design, light, scale, aspect).

Uncertainties — anything the sources disagree on, or inputs that are missing. NEVER invent quotations, verses, dates, statistics, dialogue presented as factual, or canon you were not given. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly. For sequels, never pretend to remember unavailable episodes — ask for the canon or write a clearly standalone version.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source/canon fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

PRODUCTION-LEVEL VISUAL STANDARD (MANDATORY FOR EVERY IMAGE AND VIDEO PROMPT)
Every image_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of 70–120 words — never a one-line description. Every video_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of 90–150 words describing ONE continuous achievable shot. ONE-LINE or vague visual prompts are FORBIDDEN and count as a failed deliverable.

Each image prompt MUST cover: (1) exact subject + story moment with full continuity descriptors repeated verbatim (never "same as before"), (2) readable pose, expression and interaction matching its narration segment (using faceless/anonymous/environmental framing by default for real people), (3) setting with era/materials, foreground/background depth and scale, (4) deliberate shot size + camera angle, varied every scene, (5) lighting direction + time of day + palette + the episode's locked visual treatment, (6) correct aspect composition (16:9 landscape) with key props and subjects clear of caption/UI zones, (7) a concise negative instruction inside the SAME prompt (no text/captions/logos/watermarks, no extra limbs, no duplicated subjects, no distorted faces, no style drift, no period- or canon-inappropriate objects).

Each video prompt MUST cover: stable opening composition with full continuity details, ONE clear subject action with believable progression across the stated seconds, ONE restrained camera move (or explicitly locked camera), persistent lighting/wardrobe/anatomy/props, a stable ending frame that cuts cleanly, and explicit temporal constraints (no cuts, morphing, face drift, flicker, costume changes, warped hands, disappearing props, lip-sync, dialogue, captions, watermarks).

BANNED: "Temple at sunset, cinematic light."

REQUIRED: full shootable specifics a generator can actually render — who, wearing what, doing what, where exactly, which light from which direction, which framing, which foreground/background layers, which mood.

HOOK EVERY TIME: the opening scene (and thumbnail/cover frame) must work as a scroll-stopper — a strong physical predicament, dramatic silhouette or decisive story instant with clean framing and documentary depth. No channel intros, generic greetings, or summaries before the hook.

Self-check before returning: count the words of EVERY image_prompt (expand any under 60 words with concrete visual detail) and EVERY video_prompt (expand any under 80 words with action beats, camera behavior, and ending-frame description). Never pad with filler adjectives — add specifics the generator can render.

🧭 AGAINST THE ODDS — EXTRAORDINARY TRUE STORIES
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 3.0 (Hybrid Dynamic-Tag Edition)
LONG — IMAGE + VIDEO — Bible + Script Prompt + Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, with the Dynamic Tag System
A complete horizontal documentary combining narration, still images, meaningful video clips, maps and evidence-led explanation. It is not a stretched Short.

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL
The pipeline uses three and only three functional tag families:

Narration Tag: <script>...</script> — Houses the complete, raw, TTS-ready English audio narration in Section 2B.

Auto-Incrementing Visual Tags: Sequential visual prompts matching the exact timeline order across both static and moving formats:

<image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]> for static frames.

<video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]> for motion shots.

Chronological Index Rule: The index counter [N] increments chronologically across the entire video regardless of asset type: e.g., <video_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, <video_prompt3>, <image_prompt4>.

Thumbnail Tag: Always locked strictly to <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>. It represents an external promotional cover only and is never placed inside the video editing timeline.

THIS FILE IS STANDALONE. Use only this format's template for an episode. It contains its own Bible, script pass and asset pass. No other template is required.

LOCKED FORMAT: LONG — IMAGE + VIDEO. RUNTIME: 12–18 minutes by default; 8–25 minutes when the verified story supports it; the run request Target duration (180–1200s) overrides this default. NARRATION: Simple English. ASPECT: 16:9 for playback; a separate optional 16:9 promotional thumbnail.

SOURCE FIRST: No invented facts, dialogue, people, countdowns or rescue attempts.

RETENTION FIRST: Clear immediate stakes, consequential progress, useful intermediate payoffs and a complete ending.

SCRIPT STATUS: DRAFT → READY FOR REVIEW → LOCKED only after explicit approval. Production cannot modify the locked script. Estimated timing must be replaced after rendered narration.

📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS
WORKFLOW GUIDE — how to use this file

THE BIBLE — static reference: people, locations, visual style, documentary accuracy, negative prompt, style tags

SCRIPT PROMPT — creative pass: run first

PRODUCTION PROMPT — asset pass: run second

PART 1 — 🧭 WORKFLOW GUIDE
How to Use the Split System
THE THREE WORKING PARTS
THE BIBLE: Stable channel rules plus episode-specific verified people, locations, objects and timeline. Use alongside both passes.

THE SCRIPT PROMPT: Take source-backed content and output Sections 1, 2 and 2B. This is a draft for review, wrapped in <script>...</script>.

THE PRODUCTION PROMPT: Take the explicitly locked script and Bible; output chronologically ordered visual prompts (<image_prompt[N]> and <video_prompt[N]>), overlays and publishing metadata without changing narration.

WORKFLOW PER VIDEO
STEP 1: PREPARE INPUTS
Plaintext
Type: A (Survival / Escape Story) or B (Rescue / Incident Investigation)
Format: LONG — IMAGE + VIDEO [fixed in this template]
Title: [Optional working title]
Target Duration: [12–18 minutes by default; 8–25 minutes when the verified story supports it; the run request Target duration (180–1200s) overrides this default]
Content: [Case summary supported by the supplied evidence]
Sources:
S01 | [Title] | [Author/authority] | [Date] | [URL] | [Relevant page/section]
S02 | [Title] | [Author/authority] | [Date] | [URL] | [Relevant page/section]
Source Excerpts: [Relevant passages or full accessible reports]
Confirmed Facts: [Known chronology, names, locations, durations and outcome]
Uncertain / Disputed Details: [List explicitly; NONE if none known]
Episode Bible: [Fill relevant records from Part 2]
TTS Mode: PLAIN [default] or V2_SSML [only when selected model supports it]
Visual Approach: FACELESS [default] or VERIFIED_REFERENCE
Video Clip Budget: 8 [default; change only with an explicit production reason]
Channel Handle: [Confirmed handle; NONE until selected]
CTA: REQUIRED — One brief varied English invitation to like, subscribe to Against the Odds, and leave one respectful case-specific comment after the complete verified outcome, within the selected runtime.

If source contents are missing, request the essential evidence or, when research tools are available, locate credible sources and record them before writing. Do not claim a link was read when it was not. A title or another video's transcript alone is not proof of an event.

STEP 2: RUN SCRIPT PROMPT
Paste Part 2 + Part 3 + the input packet. Receive Sections 1, 2 and 2B. Review factual accuracy, emotional pacing, and clean script boundaries. Lock only when verified.

STEP 3: RUN PRODUCTION PROMPT
Paste Part 2 + Part 4 + locked Sections 1, 2 and 2B + any asset constraints. Receive Sections 3, 4 and 5.

Section 3 generates <image_prompt0> for the 16:9 thumbnail, followed by sequentially incremented <image_prompt[N]> and <video_prompt[N]> tags in timeline playback order.

STEP 4: GENERATE AND ASSEMBLE
Extract the text inside <script>; do not send its outer tags to ElevenLabs.

For long scripts, split the extracted payload at natural paragraph boundaries to meet the selected service's input limit. Keep one master script block and a separate chunk manifest; do not omit, overlap or repeat words between chunks.

Generate a short narration test. Check names, pauses, voice and pacing before rendering the full episode.

Extract prompt payloads from <image_prompt[N]> and <video_prompt[N]> wrappers; packaging IDs must not appear as accidental image lettering.

Generate visuals; verify crop, period accuracy, geography and objects. Text must be proofread; repair unreadable text in the editor.

Render permitted motion. Add reconstruction labels in the editor; never rely only on generated lettering for disclosures.

Assemble narration and assets in strict chronological index order; replace estimated timestamps with actual timings. Never place <image_prompt0> on the video timeline.

STEP 5: FINAL LOCK
Keep the master script, final audio, prompt ID list, source ledger, asset licences and final edit together. If narration changes, create a new script version and regenerate affected timestamps, prompts and overlays. Never mix two script versions.

PART 2 — 🧭 THE BIBLE
Static Reference + Episode Records
📺 CHANNEL IDENTITY
Name: Against the Odds.

Tagline: Extraordinary stories. Impossible odds.

Language: English.

Subject: True survival, danger, escapes, rescues and human endurance.

Viewer promise: Understand the danger, follow the decisions and setbacks, and learn how the outcome became possible.

Voice: Calm, gripping, compassionate, specific and evidence-led.

Brand: Charcoal navy #101D29, warm ivory #F4EBDD, burnt orange #F07835.

Scope: Wilderness, ocean, mountains, caves, isolation and disaster survival. Technical explanations support the human story; they do not replace it.

No default recurring protagonist. Each real case has its own episode Bible.

👤 CHARACTER / PEOPLE BIBLE
Fill only evidence-backed personal details. When unknown, write UNKNOWN. Do not infer ethnicity, age, facial features, injuries or clothing from a name or country.

Plaintext
PERSON ID: P01
Verified Name / Role:
Age at Event: [Verified or UNKNOWN]
Documented Appearance: [Source-backed or UNKNOWN]
Documented Clothing / Equipment: [Source-backed or UNKNOWN]

Unknowns / Do Not Invent:
Sources:
Default FACELESS strategy: Show geography, equipment, silhouettes, distant figures, back views and non-identifying close-ups. Do not repeatedly generate the survivor's face. Even anonymous figures must have supported counts, equipment and actions. Use an environment-only frame when these details are unknown.

🗺️ LOCATION BIBLE
Plaintext

🎒 OBJECT / EQUIPMENT BIBLE
Plaintext

Verified Model or General Type:
Approximate Dimensions / Colour: [Only when supported]

A raft, jacket, rope or torch should not change colour, type or condition arbitrarily between frames. If evidence lacks detail, use a neutral schematic or omit the object rather than inventing a specific model.

🕒 TIMELINE AND EVIDENCE BIBLE
Plaintext
BEAT ID: B01
Date / Elapsed Time:
Event / Decision:
People and Location IDs:
What Was Known Then:
What Was Learned Later:
Claim Status: VERIFIED / ATTRIBUTED / DISPUTED / UNKNOWN
Source IDs + Page/Section:
Consequence:
Keep elapsed time separate from calendar dates. Distinguish what the person knew from what search teams knew. Do not narrate later findings as information available during the event.

🎨 VISUAL STYLE BIBLE
Cinematic documentary realism for environments; clear maps and diagrams for explanations.

Dark navy/ivory/orange brand system for graphics and CTA assets.

Natural, story-accurate illumination for reconstructions. No compulsory storms or orange sunsets.

Compose every frame around one useful idea and readable focal point.

Playback: 16:9. Optional promotional thumbnail: 16:9.

Prefer maps, terrain, distances, shelter, signals, search areas and objects over repeated face close-ups.

Generated assets are illustrative reconstructions, not archive footage or proof.

Add factual labels and map text in the video editor when generated text is unreliable.

⚠️ DOCUMENTARY ACCURACY LAW — NON-NEGOTIABLE
Never invent a survivor, event, dialogue, quote, thought, rescue attempt, injury, exact time or causal link.

Use exact quotations only when sourced; otherwise paraphrase and attribute.

Show fear or exhaustion through verified circumstances or attributed testimony. Do not assert unrecorded inner thoughts.

Preserve factual qualifications: estimates remain estimates and disputed accounts remain disputed.

Do not change the outcome for suspense. If an incident includes deaths or unresolved missing people, state the supported outcome respectfully.

Do not use a generated face as an authentic portrait of a real survivor.

Do not invent or dramatize evidence such as rescue recordings, report pages or satellite photos.

Label reconstruction, illustrative footage and not-to-scale diagrams where needed.

Never imply a survival action is universal advice. Describe the documented action in its context.

Rights and source credibility are separate: an accessible image still needs a valid usage basis.

Omit graphic injury imagery; focus on danger, decisions, endurance and rescue.

🔒 CONSISTENCY LAW
Each image and video prompt must include the relevant locked descriptions for every visible recurring person, location and object. Repeat them inside the prompt; do not say “same as before.” For faceless images, preserve environment and equipment continuity. The law does not force identifiable faces.

🖼️ UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE PROMPT
For photorealistic reconstructions: cartoon, anime, fantasy, supernatural rescue, gore, graphic wounds, sensational suffering, invented evidence, fake archival appearance, incorrect geography, period-inaccurate equipment, unsupported weather, extra people, duplicate limbs, deformed anatomy, inconsistent objects, illegible lettering, watermark, logos, unintended text, plastic skin, exaggerated disaster scale, morphing faces, flickering frames.

For maps/diagrams, remove the “illustration” restriction: clear schematic graphics are intended. Replace anatomy exclusions with incorrect route, invented distance, inconsistent scale, unreadable symbols and misleading orientation. Explicit thumbnail/CTA text is exempt from the unintended-text exclusion.

🖼️ UNIVERSAL STYLE TAGS
Reconstruction: cinematic documentary realism, physically plausible environment, story-accurate period and terrain, natural textures, restrained contrast, [verified lighting], [episode colour treatment], 16:9 landscape aspect, clear focal point, high-detail image.

Map/diagram: clean documentary graphic, navy background, ivory labels, orange route accents, simple readable geometry, [verified geography], uncluttered composition, 16:9 landscape aspect.

[AGAINST THE ODDS EDITORIAL RULES]
These rules update Against the Odds' research, narration, ending and engagement instructions below. Preserve the existing English language, output sections, extraction tags, asset numbering, media modes, visual style, faceless depiction policy, reconstruction disclosures and exact narration-to-scene mapping. Work silently and use the existing evidence/production sections; do not add a new editorial-analysis section.

VERIFY THE STORY BEFORE COMMITTING TO THE HOOK: Establish the documented predicament, actual people, place, chronology, available resources, failed options, decisive action and supported outcome. Tie material claims to identifiable sources in the existing evidence notes; prefer investigation/rescue reports, expedition records and attributed firsthand accounts, with reliable corroboration where available. Separate documented facts, estimates, disputed accounts, attributed recollections and unknowns. An encyclopedia snippet or model recollection alone is not proof of a precise claim. Treat a preselected hook as provisional and revise unsupported promises. If a material gap blocks a factual account, use the template's existing research-required process; never fill it with fiction.

OPEN AT THE VERIFIED PREDICAMENT: Compare three source-supported openings internally: immediate danger, an obvious escape that failed, and a surprising documented constraint. Select the clearest one a new viewer can understand without the title. Start with a short factual sentence naming the person or group and the concrete problem; the first visual must show that same predicament, equipment or geography. The next sentence supplies an actual constraint, action or consequence rather than restarting with biography, a location lecture or a topic introduction. No invented countdown, superlative, quotation, private thought, last breath or rescue uncertainty. Do not imply the outcome is unknown when it is established; suspense can come from how the documented result became possible.

CAUSE AND EFFECT, NOT SENSATIONALISM: Follow danger -> constrained choices -> documented attempts/setbacks -> decisive action or assistance -> verified outcome. Each sentence must add necessary context, a resource constraint, an action, new evidence, a changed option or a consequence. Explain why an option was unavailable only when the sources support that link. Track what survivors and rescuers knew at each point; do not give one group another's information prematurely. Attribute testimony naturally. Use simple spoken English, concrete verbs, clear subjects and emotional breaths. Cut repeated danger descriptions, repeated praise, decorative geography and generic inspirational morals. Do not exaggerate injuries, suffering, weather, distances, durations, casualty counts or the scale of a disaster. Never turn a documented survival action into universal medical or survival advice.

LONG VIDEOS: Use the selected long-form runtime and develop connected factual questions across the existing chapters. Each chapter must explain an attempt, resource change, search difficulty, discovery or consequential decision, answer its immediate question and advance the chronology. Bring in background when it explains the next action; do not restart the introduction or recap the danger at every chapter. Reorder exposition only when it does not misrepresent the actual sequence or what people knew. Give useful intermediate answers and show the decisive action, rescue/assistance and full supported outcome before the close.

EARN THE ENDING: State what actually happened, including uncertainty, fatalities, unresolved missing people or later consequences when relevant and supported. Do not force a triumphant ending or imply willpower alone caused survival. Credit documented help and circumstance. End the story on a concrete consequence or detail whose significance is now clear; no withheld answer, invented next-episode tease or repeated moral. Keep generated visuals identifiable as reconstructions, not archival evidence. Do not invent a real person's face, actions, dialogue or equipment to make the hook more dramatic.

ONE VARIED ENGAGEMENT CLOSE: After the complete outcome, include ONE compact English invitation to like the video, subscribe to Against the Odds and leave ONE case-specific comment. Reserve approximately 8–12 seconds within the selected runtime. This replaces the legacy optional subscribe-only CTA. Use the existing final narration/follow/end-card slots as one close, without repeating the engagement speech or adding silent padding. Keep its tone proportionate to the real event, especially when people died or remain missing.

VARY THE COMMENT INVITATION: Ask one concrete, respectful question about a documented turning point, constraint, resource, rescue contribution or surprising verified detail. Vary the question and sentence structure with the case, rather than always asking 'Would you survive?' or demanding the same slogan. Do not ask viewers to judge a survivor's worth, blame victims, repeat dangerous actions, disclose trauma or compete over suffering. Align the pinned comment with the spoken question; do not pile on extra questions or ask for repeated comments. The verified answer must never depend on likes, comments or subscriptions.

Example patterns to adapt only when the facts support them: 'Which decision made rescue possible? Comment below, and like and subscribe for more Against the Odds stories.' / 'What surprised you most about the search? Tell us below. Like the video and subscribe for more documented stories.' / 'Which mattered more here: the signal or the search? Leave your choice below, and like and subscribe.' Replace broad wording with the actual decision, resource or detail when possible. Do not invent facts to fit an example, use guilt or false rewards, or import devotional slogans or fictional rule-breaking language.

FINAL SILENT CHECK: The hook and its next sentence advance the same verified predicament; important claims have sources; uncertainties remain qualified; chronology and knowledge states are accurate; every beat adds information; the outcome fully answers the opening promise before the CTA. Closing words contain like + subscribe + one varied case-specific comment invitation, within the selected runtime, exactly once in the clean script and matching final CTA narration segment(s). Preserve all original tags, overlay sections and reconstruction safeguards. Do not output these checks or predict audience retention scores.
[/AGAINST THE ODDS EDITORIAL RULES]

PART 3 — 🧭 SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)
Your ONLY job is to turn supplied, verified content into an English script for review. Do not generate visual prompts in this pass. Scene descriptions are high-level editorial guidance only.

⚙️ STEP 0 — CONTENT ANALYSIS (SILENT)
Identify content type, format, central question, verified outcome, primary emotion, chronology, people, locations, equipment, strongest documented reversal, feasible runtime and source gaps.

If missing evidence blocks a factual account, return RESEARCH REQUIRED with the specific missing claims and sources needed. Do not fill the gaps with fiction. Silent analysis does not mean hiding material uncertainty: report it in the evidence ledger.

❤️ EMOTION EXTRACTION LAW
Choose one dominant emotion: tension, isolation, hope, courage, relief, grief or awe. Let secondary emotions develop as circumstances change.

Ask: “What makes these verified circumstances meaningful to a person?” Show concrete stakes such as distance, weather, limited supplies, communication failure or search difficulty. Facts and emotion work together. Do not replace useful detail with vague inspirational language.

🎯 HOOK RULES — STAKES + A SPECIFIC QUESTION
The first spoken line introduces real danger and a question worth resolving. Use a clear first sentence that immediately establishes danger; no word-count trick. Within 20–30 seconds establish the person, predicament and documentary question.

Formula: Verified danger + unresolved decision or outcome mechanism.

Illustrative patterns, not factual case claims:

“The search ended. He was still alive.” [Only if supported.]

“Their boat was gone. Land was nowhere in sight.”

“The exit was underwater.”

“They survived the crash. Then the cold arrived.”

The hook must be the first spoken line. Never start with “Welcome back,” “Today we will talk about,” the channel name or an episode number. Do not use unsupported superlatives, invented countdowns or false mysteries.

🎯 MANDATORY NARRATION OPENING STRUCTURE
Plaintext
[EMOTIONAL / DANGER HOOK]

[SHORT NATURAL PAUSE]

[STORY BEGINS IMMEDIATELY]
🎯 MIDPOINT RE-HOOK RULE
Place one primary re-hook near 50–60% of the planned runtime when a documented reversal supports it. Keep it concise and supported. Use other consequential turning points throughout the documentary; do not add artificial cliffhangers on a fixed timer.

If no new reversal exists at that point, frame a still-unresolved factual problem rather than inventing an event. Reordering exposition is allowed; reordering the actual chronology in a misleading way is not.

📜 SECTION 1 — SCRIPT BREAKDOWN (Production Planning)
LANGUAGE: Simple English, short clear sentences, natural documentary narration.

DURATION: 12–18 minutes by default; 8–25 minutes when supported. Estimate narration at roughly 130–150 words per minute plus intentional visual pauses; actual rendered audio is authoritative.

📲 COMPLETE ENDING — AFTER THE STORY IS COMPLETE
Resolve the survival/rescue question and state the supported outcome.

Include relevant aftermath without turning the episode into generic life advice.

After the complete supported outcome, give ONE compact English close asking for like, subscribe and one respectful case-specific comment. Reserve approximately 8–12 seconds within the selected runtime, following the editorial rules above.

Keep all three engagement requests in that single close; no repeated engagement speech or invented next-episode tease.

🎙️ SECTION 2 — ELEVENLABS TTS SCRIPT (WITH TIMESTAMPS)

Preserve every spoken word from Section 1 in exactly the same order.

🎙️ SECTION 2B — ELEVENLABS COMPLETE VOICED SCRIPT (PASTE-READY)

Rules for <script> Tag:

Exactly one block per episode.

Spoken words only. NO timestamps, scene titles, speaker tags, markdown formatting, (break), or parenthesized emotion tags like (whisper) or (tense).

Strip outer tags before pasting into ElevenLabs.

PART 4 — 🧭 PRODUCTION PROMPT (Asset Pass — Run SECOND)
Your ONLY job is to generate asset prompts and engagement metadata for a LOCKED script. Do not rewrite, shorten, expand or reorder its narration.

🖼️ SECTION 3 — VISUAL GENERATION PROMPTS (CHRONOLOGICAL TIMELINE)
Prompts MUST follow exact chronological sequence. The index increments across all media:

<image_prompt0>: 16:9 Promotional Thumbnail (Strictly external cover; never placed in playback timeline).

<image_prompt1> to <image_prompt[N]> / <video_prompt1> to <video_prompt[N]>: Story scenes, Follow Frame, and End Card in planned timeline playback order.

For 12–18 minutes, start with approximately 40–70 meaningful scene stills/maps/diagrams and 8 selected video clips of roughly 4–8 usable seconds. Plan at least ceiling(targetSeconds/10) scenes (18 for 180s, 30 for 300s, 60 for 600s, 90 for 900s, 120 for 1200s, capped at 160). Increase assets when actual coverage needs it.

Format Standards:

Five of these Chiranjeevis are designated to take up administrative roles in the upcoming Savarni Manvantara. In Hindu philosophy, physical immortality is never confused with ultimate liberation, or Moksha. Living for millions of years within physical time is still a form of bondage to the material realm. True freedom is transcending time altogether.

विद्वान इन स्थानीय कथाओं और मूल संस्कृत ग्रंथों के अंतर को स्पष्ट करते हैं।

लेकिन अश्वत्थामा उन सात अमर विभूतियों में से केवल एक है।

अश्वत्थामा के अलावा बाकी छह चिरंजीवी कलयुग में धर्म और ज्ञान की रक्षा करते हैं।

दानवीर राजा बलि ने अपने न्यायप्रिय शासन से तीनों लोकों में अपार कीर्ति प्राप्त की थी।

तब भगवान वामन ने बटुक रूप धरकर राजा बलि से तीन पग भूमि का दान मांगा।

वामन देव ने विराट रूप धारण कर दो ही पगों में पूरी पृथ्वी और आकाश नाप लिया।

उनकी दानशीलता से प्रसन्न होकर प्रभु ने उन्हें सुतल लोक का अमर स्वामी बना दिया।

भविष्य के सावर्णि मन्वंतर में राजा बलि स्वर्ग के देवराज इंद्र बनेंगे।

महर्षि वेदव्यास ने मानवता के कल्याण के लिए वेदों का चार भागों में विभाजन किया।

उन्होंने अट्ठारह पुराण और अमर महाकाव्य महाभारत की रचना कर ज्ञान को सुरक्षित किया।

परंपरा मानती है कि बद्रीनाथ के निकट माणा गांव की व्यास गुफा में वे आज भी उपस्थित हैं।

हिमालय की इन पावन कंदराओं में उनकी तपस्या का प्रभाव आज भी महसूस किया जाता है।

पवनपुत्र हनुमान जी ने प्रभु श्रीराम के बैकुंठ गमन के समय पृथ्वी पर ही रहना चुना।

मान्यता है कि जहां भी रामकथा का गुणगान होता है, वहां हनुमान जी सशरीर उपस्थित रहते हैं।

गंधमादन पर्वत पर ध्यानमग्न रहकर वे कलयुग के अंत तक भक्तों की रक्षा करते हैं।

लंकापति रावण के अधर्म का विरोध कर विभीषण ने श्रीराम की शरण स्वीकार की थी।

रावण के वध के बाद श्रीराम ने विभीषण को लंका का अमर राजा घोषित किया।

विभीषण ने कुल मोह छोड़कर केवल सत्य और सनातन धर्म का साथ दिया था।

वरदान के अनुसार, विभीषण कल्प के अंत तक धर्मपूर्वक लंका पर शासन करते रहेंगे।

कौरवों और पांडवों के कुलगुरु कृपाचार्य परम तपस्वी और अजेय धनुर्धर रहे हैं।

शास्त्रों के अनुसार, कलयुग के अंत में वे भगवान कल्कि को दिव्य अस्त्र-शस्त्रों की दीक्षा देंगे।

भगवान परशुराम भगवान विष्णु के छठे आवेशावतार हैं, जिनका तेज आज भी असीम है।

उन्होंने अपने दिव्य फरसे से इक्कीस बार अत्याचारी राजाओं का मानमर्दन किया था।

कलयुग के अंत में वे पुनः प्रकट होकर भगवान कल्कि के मुख्य मार्गदर्शक और गुरु बनेंगे।

ये सभी चिरंजीवी सनातन सत्य और ईश्वरीय विधान को बनाए रखने के लिए धरती पर स्थित हैं।

महामृत्युंजय मंत्र के ज्ञाता ऋषि मार्कंडेय ने भी शिव भक्ति से काल को पराजित किया था।

शास्त्रों के अनुसार, यह कोई साधारण घाव नहीं, बल्कि बिना मृत्यु के मिलने वाला अनंत दंड है।

हमारी धरती पर सात ऐसे अमर चिरंजीवी हैं, जिन्हें कलयुग के अंत तक जीवित रहना है।

इस भयानक गाथा की शुरुआत महाभारत युद्ध की अट्ठारहवीं रात को हुई थी।

अट्ठारह दिनों के भीषण नरसंहार के बाद कुरुक्षेत्र का मैदान आधी रात में शांत पड़ा था।

हजारों योद्धाओं के शव और उनके लोहे के कवच ठंडी चांदनी में चमक रहे थे।

अपने पिता द्रोणाचार्य के वध से क्रोधित अश्वत्थामा बदले की आग में जल रहा था।

रात के अंधेरे में उल्लू को शिकार करते देख उसने युद्ध के सारे नियम तोड़ दिए।

पांडवों के सोते हुए शिविर में घुसकर उसने द्रौपदी के पांच मासूम पुत्रों का वध कर दिया।

सुबह होते ही इस जघन्य पाप को देखकर पांडव और श्रीकृष्ण अत्यंत क्रोधित हो उठे।

गंगा तट पर जब अर्जुन और श्रीकृष्ण ने अश्वत्थामा को घेरा, तो उसके बचने का कोई मार्ग न था।

घबराकर अश्वत्थामा ने तिनके को अभिमंत्रित कर प्रलयंकारी ब्रह्माशिरा अस्त्र छोड़ दिया।

इस अस्त्र की प्रचंड ज्वाला पूरी सृष्टि को भस्म करने के लिए आगे बढ़ी।

सृष्टि की रक्षा के लिए अर्जुन ने भी अपना ब्रह्माशिरा अस्त्र प्रकट कर दिया।

तभी महर्षि व्यास और नारद जी ने बीच में आकर दोनों को अस्त्र वापस लेने का आदेश दिया।

अर्जुन ने अपने अस्त्र को तुरंत शांत कर वापस अपने गांडीव में समेट लिया।

लेकिन अस्त्र लौटाने में असमर्थ अश्वत्थामा ने उसे उत्तरा के गर्भ की ओर मोड़ दिया।

उस दिव्य अस्त्र के तेज से उत्तरा के गर्भ में पल रहा बालक परीक्षित निष्प्राण हो गया।

तब भगवान श्रीकृष्ण ने अपने सत्य और योगबल से उस मृत बालक को पुनः जीवन दिया।

इसके बाद श्रीकृष्ण ने अश्वत्थामा की ओर मुड़कर एक ऐसा ऐतिहासिक न्याय सुनाया।

उन्होंने अश्वत्थामा को मृत्यु नहीं दी, बल्कि तीन हजार वर्षों तक निर्जन भटकने का शाप दिया।

बिना किसी साथी के, वह दुर्गम जंगलों में लहूलुहान होकर भटकता रहेगा।

श्रीकृष्ण के आदेश पर अश्वत्थामा के मस्तक से उसकी जन्मजात दिव्य शिरोमणि छीन ली गई।

यह मणि उसे भूख, प्यास, रोग और अस्त्र-शस्त्रों से सुरक्षित रखती थी।

मणि निकलते ही उसके माथे का घाव हमेशा के लिए रिसता हुआ नासूर बन गया।

महाभारत के सौप्तिक पर्व में स्पष्ट लिखा है कि उसका यह घाव कभी नहीं भरेगा।

आज भी मध्य प्रदेश के असीरगढ़ किले और नर्मदा तट पर उसके देखे जाने के दावे किए जाते हैं।

विद्वान इन स्थानीय कथाओं और मूल संस्कृत ग्रंथों के अंतर को स्पष्ट करते हैं।

लेकिन अश्वत्थामा उन सात अमर विभूतियों में से केवल एक है।

चिरंजीवी श्लोक में अश्वत्थामा, बलि, व्यास, हनुमान, विभीषण, कृपाचार्य और परशुराम का नाम आता है।

अश्वत्थामा के अलावा बाकी छह चिरंजीवी कलयुग में धर्म और ज्ञान की रक्षा करते हैं।

दानवीर राजा बलि ने अपने न्यायप्रिय शासन से तीनों लोकों में अपार कीर्ति प्राप्त की थी।

तब भगवान वामन ने बटुक रूप धरकर राजा बलि से तीन पग भूमि का दान मांगा।

वामन देव ने विराट रूप धारण कर दो ही पगों में पूरी पृथ्वी और आकाश नाप लिया।

तीसरे पग के लिए राजा बलि ने विनम्रता से अपना मस्तक आगे कर दिया।

उनकी दानशीलता से प्रसन्न होकर प्रभु ने उन्हें सुतल लोक का अमर स्वामी बना दिया।

भविष्य के सावर्णि मन्वंतर में राजा बलि स्वर्ग के देवराज इंद्र बनेंगे।

महर्षि वेदव्यास ने मानवता के कल्याण के लिए वेदों का चार भागों में विभाजन किया।

उन्होंने अट्ठारह पुराण और अमर महाकाव्य महाभारत की रचना कर ज्ञान को सुरक्षित किया।

परंपरा मानती है कि बद्रीनाथ के निकट माणा गांव की व्यास गुफा में वे आज भी उपस्थित हैं।

हिमालय की इन पावन कंदराओं में उनकी तपस्या का प्रभाव आज भी महसूस किया जाता है।

पवनपुत्र हनुमान जी ने प्रभु श्रीराम के बैकुंठ गमन के समय पृथ्वी पर ही रहना चुना।

मान्यता है कि जहां भी रामकथा का गुणगान होता है, वहां हनुमान जी सशरीर उपस्थित रहते हैं।

गंधमादन पर्वत पर ध्यानमग्न रहकर वे कलयुग के अंत तक भक्तों की रक्षा करते हैं।

लंकापति रावण के अधर्म का विरोध कर विभीषण ने श्रीराम की शरण स्वीकार की थी।

रावण के वध के बाद श्रीराम ने विभीषण को लंका का अमर राजा घोषित किया।

विभीषण ने कुल मोह छोड़कर केवल सत्य और सनातन धर्म का साथ दिया था।

वरदान के अनुसार, विभीषण कल्प के अंत तक धर्मपूर्वक लंका पर शासन करते रहेंगे।

कौरवों और पांडवों के कुलगुरु कृपाचार्य परम तपस्वी और अजेय धनुर्धर रहे हैं।

शास्त्रों के अनुसार, कलयुग के अंत में वे भगवान कल्कि को दिव्य अस्त्र-शस्त्रों की दीक्षा देंगे।

भगवान परशुराम भगवान विष्णु के छठे आवेशावतार हैं, जिनका तेज आज भी असीम है।

उन्होंने अपने दिव्य फरसे से इक्कीस बार अत्याचारी राजाओं का मानमर्दन किया था।

वर्तमान में वे महेंद्रगिरि पर्वत की गुप्त गुफाओं में तपस्यारत हैं।

कलयुग के अंत में वे पुनः प्रकट होकर भगवान कल्कि के मुख्य मार्गदर्शक और गुरु बनेंगे।

ये सभी चिरंजीवी सनातन सत्य और ईश्वरीय विधान को बनाए रखने के लिए धरती पर स्थित हैं।

महामृत्युंजय मंत्र के ज्ञाता ऋषि मार्कंडेय ने भी शिव भक्ति से काल को पराजित किया था।

जहाँ छह चिरंजीवी सेवा और तपस्या का प्रतीक हैं, वहीं अश्वत्थामा अहंकार के दुष्परिणाम का प्रमाण है।

अमरता यदि वरदान हो तो कल्याणकारी है, पर शाप बन जाए तो घोर पीड़ा बन जाती है।

यदि शरीर अमर हो जाए लेकिन शाप कभी न मिटे, तो क्या आप ऐसी अमरता स्वीकार करेंगे?

### Section 1: Verified Facts, Background & Key Data

#### Evidence Ledger & Source Verification
This documentary dossier investigates the concept of *Chiranjeevis* (immortals/long-lived beings) in Hindu scriptural canon, contrasting popular modern perceptions of eternal life as a divine reward against the actual textual reality of physical burden, cosmic duty, and punitive agony.

| Fact / Canonical Claim | Primary Source & Citation | Verification & Context Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ashwatthama's Nocturnal Massacre** | *Mahabharata*, Sauptika Parva (Book 10, Ch. 1–9) | On the 18th night of the Kurukshetra war, Ashwatthama, Kripa, and Kritavarma infiltrate the sleeping Pandava camp. Ashwatthama slaughters Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandi, and the five sleeping sons of Draupadi (*Upapandavas*). |
| **Invocation & Diversion of Brahmashira Astra** | *Mahabharata*, Sauptika Parva (Book 10, Ch. 13–15) | Cornered by the Pandavas and Krishna on the banks of the Ganga at Vyasa’s hermitage, Ashwatthama hurls the apocalyptic *Brahmashira* weapon using a blade of grass. Arjuna counters with his own *Brahmashira*. Sages Vyasa and Narada intervene to halt global catastrophe. Arjuna withdraws his weapon; Ashwatthama lacks the knowledge to retract his and redirects it into the womb of Uttara to extinguish the Pandava lineage. |
| **Krishna's Divine Intervention & Revitalization** | *Mahabharata*, Sauptika Parva (Book 10, Ch. 16, Verses 8–15) | Krishna vows that although Uttara's fetus (*Parikshit*) will be born stillborn from the astral radiation, Krishna will revive him through his austerities and truth, allowing the royal Kuru lineage to survive. |
| **The Precise Sentence & Forehead Wound Curse** | *Mahabharata*, Sauptika Parva (Book 10, Ch. 16, Verses 9–21); *Bhagavata Purana* (1.7.50–55) | Krishna curses Ashwatthama: he will roam the Earth for 3,000 years (or across yugas) completely isolated, smelling of blood and pus, afflicted by every severe disease, with no human companion or ability to converse. |
| **Extraction of the Divine Mani (Jewel)** | *Mahabharata*, Sauptika Parva (Book 10, Ch. 16, Verses 25–35) | Ashwatthama surrendered the innate jewel (*Shiron Mani*) on his forehead. The jewel previously shielded him from hunger, thirst, physical fatigue, disease, weapons, and divine/demonic entities. Deprived of the jewel, the wound left on his forehead remains open, oozing blood and pus incessantly while denied the release of death. |
| **Canonical List of the 7 Chiranjeevis** | Classical *Cirañjīvi Stotram* (*aśvatthāmā balirvyāso...*) | The seven recognized immortals are: Ashwatthama, King Mahabali, Veda Vyasa, Hanuman, Vibhishana, Kripacharya, and Parashurama (with Sage Markandeya often cited as an eighth). |
| **Cosmic Purpose: Manvantara Staffing** | *Bhagavata Purana* (Book 8, Ch. 13, Verses 12–16) | Immortality in Hindu cosmology (*Kalpa* cycle) is rarely a personal reward. Five of the Chiranjeevis (Parashurama, Ashwatthama, Kripacharya, Vyasa, and Mahabali) are held in cosmic reserve to serve as the *Saptarshis* (Seven Great Sages) and the *Indra* during the upcoming 8th *Savarni Manvantara*. |

#### Documented Canon vs. Popular Folklore
*   **Textual Evidence (Mahabharata & Bhagavata Purana)**: Ashwatthama's longevity is explicitly a curse of biological torment and total social exile following adharma. The jewel's removal strips him of physical defense against pain while leaving his life force bound to the Earth.
*   **Regional Legend & Sightings**: Modern Indian urban legends claim Ashwatthama roams the Narmada River basin or the Asirgarh Fort in Madhya Pradesh seeking oil to heal his bleeding head wound. *Dossier Directive*: These modern folklore claims must be identified strictly as post-scriptural oral legends, keeping clear distinction from the Sanskrit text of the *Sauptika Parva*.
*   **Immortality (*Amaratva*) vs. Aeon-Bound Longevity (*Cirañjīvin*)**: Scriptural *amaratva* (absolute immortality beyond cosmic dissolution) is distinct from *cirañjīvin* (living for a long duration/aeon until the end of a cosmic cycle or *Manvantara*).

---

### Section 2: Chronological Story Arc & Scene Beats (~1200s)

#### Overview & Structure
*   **Total Duration**: ~1200 seconds (20:00).
*   **Narrative Arc**: Verified predicament (The curse of unending physical suffering) $\rightarrow$ Constrained choices (The nocturnal slaughter at Kurukshetra) $\rightarrow$ Setbacks & Escalation (Unleashing apocalyptic weaponry) $\rightarrow$ Decisive Intervention (Krishna's judgment and jewel extraction) $\rightarrow$ Verified Outcome & Cosmic Reality (The 7 Chiranjeevis as duty-bound cosmic stewards across Kali Yuga) $\rightarrow$ Varied English Close.

```
[00:00 - 02:00]  ACT I: THE BLEEDING IMMORTAL (Opening Predicament & Hook)
[02:00 - 06:00]  ACT II: THE CRIMSON NIGHT & THE APOCALYPTIC WEAPON (Kurukshetra Aftermath)
[06:00 - 10:00]  ACT III: KRISHNA'S CURSE & THE DE-JEWELED WOUND (Earned Payoff: Sauptika Parva)
[10:00 - 15:00]  ACT IV: THE SEVEN STEWARDS OF KALI YUGA (Comparing the 7 Chiranjeevis)
[15:00 - 19:48]  ACT V: IMMORTALITY AS A SENTENCE (Cosmic Manvantara Reality & Outcome)
[19:48 - 20:00]  ACT VI: ENGLISH ENGAGEMENT CLOSE & PINNED COMMENT ALIGNMENT
```

##### Act I: The Bleeding Immortal (00:00 – 02:00)
*   **Scene 1 (00:00 – 00:40)** `[VIDEO]`
    *   *Visual*: Opening Visual — A solitary, shadowy figure clad in ragged ancient rags walking through a dark, mist-covered forest, his face obscured, with a subtle glowing lesion on his forehead.
    *   *Narration*: "In the Sanskrit epics, Ashwatthama is not granted eternal youth; he is condemned to roam the Earth for thousands of years with a bleeding, unhealing wound on his forehead."
    *   *Constraint/Context*: The text of the *Sauptika Parva* reveals that immortality in ancient Indian tradition was not always an elixir of grace, but could be forged as an escape-proof prison.
*   **Scene 2 (00:40 – 01:20)** `[STATIC IMAGE]`
    *   *Visual*: Split composition (Thumbnail visual baseline) — An ancient palm-leaf manuscript with Sanskrit lettering illuminated by flickering oil lamp light on the left; a towering shadowed warrior silhouette standing amidst modern misty ruins on the right. Text overlay concept: "NOT A GIFT".
    *   *Narration*: Viewer Promise — Discover why immortality in Hindu canon is presented not as a divine gift, but as a grueling, physical sentence of suffering across millennia.
*   **Scene 3 (01:20 – 02:00)** `[VIDEO]`
    *   *Visual*: High-contrast cinematic tracking shot moving slowly across an abandoned ancient battlefield strewn with charred chariots, banners, and iron spears under a blood-red dawn.
    *   *Narration*: To understand the physical horror of Ashwatthama’s sentence, we must return to the 18th night of the Kurukshetra War—when a single breach of war ethics altered a warrior's fate for eternity.

##### Act II: The Crimson Night & The Apocalyptic Weapon (02:00 – 06:00)

    *   *Visual*: Close-up of three shadowy figures standing at the perimeter of a dark tent encampment; an owl attacking a nest of sleeping crows in a giant banyan tree depicted in classical Indian painting style.
    *   *Narration*: Enraged by the dishonorable killing of his father Dronacharya, Ashwatthama observed an owl ambushing sleeping crows at midnight—a natural cue he used to justify a forbidden nighttime raid.

    *   *Narration*: In the dead of night, Ashwatthama breached the sacred Kshatriya code of war, slaughtering the Panchala commanders and the five sleeping young sons of Draupadi.

    *   *Visual*: Detailed artwork of Sage Vyasa’s serene hermitage on the banks of the river Ganga, where a desperate, cornered warrior plucks a blade of grass to chant celestial incantations.

##### Video Description
> Modern popular culture often views living forever as a divine gift, but ancient Sanskrit scripture tells a far darker, more demanding story. In this deep documentary investigation, we explore the canonical reality of the **7 Chiranjeevis** (aeon-bound immortals) as recorded in the *Mahabharata*, *Bhagavata Purana*, and *Valmiki Ramayana*. 
>
> From the unhealing forehead wound of Ashwatthama following the 18th night of Kurukshetra, to the cosmic administrative duties of King Mahabali, Veda Vyasa, Hanuman, Vibhishana, Kripacharya, and Parashurama—discover why Hindu cosmology presents immortality not as luxury, but as functional cosmic staffing or escape-proof punitive exile across Kali Yuga.
>
> 📜 **Primary Sources Cited**:
> - *Mahabharata* (Sauptika Parva, Book 10)
> - *Bhagavata Purana* (Book 8, Chapter 13 & 22)
> - *Valmiki Ramayana* (Uttara Kanda & Yuddha Kanda)

prompts.name: LONG master prompt (Stickman Survival V3)
prompts.content:
### 🎨 MANDATORY STICKMAN VISUAL SPECIFICATION (APPLIED TO EVERY IMAGE & VIDEO PROMPT)
CRITICAL ART DIRECTION: Every visual prompt (<image_prompt[N]> and <video_prompt[N]>) MUST strictly follow this exact formulation so it renders as high-end concept art illustration, NOT as a realistic photo or 3D mannequin:

1. PROMPT OPENING (MANDATORY EXACT PHRASING):
- Still Images: MUST start with: "Stylized cinematic digital concept art illustration, graphic novel aesthetic, hand-painted digital art style with expressive atmospheric lighting and rich textures, [aspect ratio]."
- Video Clips: MUST start with: "Stylized cinematic continuous shot concept art animation video, graphic novel aesthetic, hand-painted digital art style with expressive atmospheric lighting and rich textures, [aspect ratio]."

2. CHARACTER DEFINITION (MANDATORY EXACT ANCHORS):
- ALWAYS describe the protagonist as: "a minimalist clean black stick figure silhouette (solid black circle head, clean slender black stick limbs, zero facial features)"
- Add iconic environment-specific survival gear:
  * Outback / Desert: "wearing tattered dust-bleached linen and carrying a dented metal canteen"
  * Blizzard / Everest: "wearing a bright hazard-yellow insulated expedition down parka and hood, climbing harness, and gripping an ice axe"
  * Ocean / Shipwreck: "wearing a high-visibility emergency orange life vest, clinging to wooden wreckage"
  * Cave / Underground: "wearing a blue/teal caving suit and safety helmet with a piercing white conical headlamp beam"
- Expressive physical posture: exhausted slouch, desperate crawl, shivering limbs, tense struggling silhouette against wind/waves.

3. ENVIRONMENT & SCALE:
- Epic, rich, cinematic landscapes: sweeping sand dunes with heat mirages; towering dark blizzard mountain saddles; colossal midnight ocean storm swells; claustrophobic flooded rock tunnels.
- Extreme scale contrast: tiny stick figure dwarfed by overwhelming, lethal natural elements.

4. BANNED WORDS (NEVER USE THESE IN PROMPTS):
- FORBIDDEN: "Documentary reconstruction", "photorealistic", "photojournalism", "35mm", "Kodak", "photograph", "realistic skin", "skin pores".

5. MANDATORY NEGATIVE PROMPT (Include verbatim in every prompt block):
"no 3D CGI render, no 3D blender models, no mannequin, no clay render, no sterile CGI gloss, no photorealistic stock photography, no real human skin, no human facial features, no cartoon slapstick, no comedic doodles, no text, no watermarks, no distorted anatomy"

6. MANDATORY STYLE TAGS:
"Stylized graphic novel and cinematic stickman animation art style, serious survival drama tone, minimalist solid black stick figure protagonist, epic atmospheric scale, dramatic lighting, high-detail landscape, no comedy, no slapstick, no photorealistic human face"


### ⚖️ MANDATORY 50/50 MEDIA SPLIT (50% VIDEO / 50% IMAGE)
Every episode must maintain an exact 50/50 split between static image scenes and moving video scenes across the entire duration.
Follow an alternating rhythm throughout the timeline (Scene 1 MUST always be a video to hook the user):
- Odd scenes (Scene 1, Scene 3, Scene 5, ...): MOTION VIDEO CLIP (<video_prompt[N]>)
- Even scenes (Scene 2, Scene 4, Scene 6, ...): STATIC IMAGE (<image_prompt[N]>)
Ensure exactly 50% of the scenes are designated as image assets and 50% as video assets.

STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image/video prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic, Source Material, and Input/Canon Packet. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently (do not output your notes unless the template asks for a packet) and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened (or, for fiction: the locked rule, canon, and inputs supplied), who is involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, popular myth, or unestablished canon.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume/design, light, scale, aspect).

Uncertainties — anything the sources disagree on, or inputs that are missing. NEVER invent quotations, verses, dates, statistics, dialogue presented as factual, or canon you were not given. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly. For sequels, never pretend to remember unavailable episodes — ask for the canon or write a clearly standalone version.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source/canon fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

PRODUCTION-LEVEL VISUAL STANDARD (MANDATORY FOR EVERY IMAGE AND VIDEO PROMPT)
Every image_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of 70–120 words — never a one-line description. Every video_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of 90–150 words describing ONE continuous achievable shot. ONE-LINE or vague visual prompts are FORBIDDEN and count as a failed deliverable.

Each image prompt MUST cover: (1) exact subject + story moment with full continuity descriptors repeated verbatim (never "same as before"), (2) readable pose, expression and interaction matching its narration segment (using faceless/anonymous/environmental framing by default for real people), (3) setting with era/materials, foreground/background depth and scale, (4) deliberate shot size + camera angle, varied every scene, (5) lighting direction + time of day + palette + the episode's locked visual treatment, (6) correct aspect composition (16:9 landscape) with key props and subjects clear of caption/UI zones, (7) a concise negative instruction inside the SAME prompt (no text/captions/logos/watermarks, no extra limbs, no duplicated subjects, no distorted faces, no style drift, no period- or canon-inappropriate objects).

Each video prompt MUST cover: stable opening composition with full continuity details, ONE clear subject action with believable progression across the stated seconds, ONE restrained camera move (or explicitly locked camera), persistent lighting/wardrobe/anatomy/props, a stable ending frame that cuts cleanly, and explicit temporal constraints (no cuts, morphing, face drift, flicker, costume changes, warped hands, disappearing props, lip-sync, dialogue, captions, watermarks).

BANNED: "Temple at sunset, cinematic light."

REQUIRED: full shootable specifics a generator can actually render — who, wearing what, doing what, where exactly, which light from which direction, which framing, which foreground/background layers, which mood.

HOOK EVERY TIME: the opening scene (and thumbnail/cover frame) must work as a scroll-stopper — a strong physical predicament, dramatic silhouette or decisive story instant with clean framing and documentary depth. No channel intros, generic greetings, or summaries before the hook.

Self-check before returning: count the words of EVERY image_prompt (expand any under 60 words with concrete visual detail) and EVERY video_prompt (expand any under 80 words with action beats, camera behavior, and ending-frame description). Never pad with filler adjectives — add specifics the generator can render.

🧭 AGAINST THE ODDS — EXTRAORDINARY TRUE STORIES
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 3.0 (Hybrid Dynamic-Tag Edition)
LONG — IMAGE + VIDEO — Bible + Script Prompt + Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, with the Dynamic Tag System
A complete horizontal documentary combining narration, still images, meaningful video clips, maps and evidence-led explanation. It is not a stretched Short.

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL
The pipeline uses three and only three functional tag families:

Narration Tag: <script>...</script> — Houses the complete, raw, TTS-ready English audio narration in Section 2B.

Auto-Incrementing Visual Tags: Sequential visual prompts matching the exact timeline order across both static and moving formats:

<image_prompt[N]>...</image_prompt[N]> for static frames.

<video_prompt[N]>...</video_prompt[N]> for motion shots.

Chronological Index Rule: The index counter [N] increments chronologically across the entire video regardless of asset type: e.g., <video_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, <video_prompt3>, <image_prompt4>.

Thumbnail Tag: Always locked strictly to <image_prompt0>...</image_prompt0>. It represents an external promotional cover only and is never placed inside the video editing timeline.

THIS FILE IS STANDALONE. Use only this format's template for an episode. It contains its own Bible, script pass and asset pass. No other template is required.

LOCKED FORMAT: LONG — IMAGE + VIDEO. RUNTIME: 12–18 minutes by default; 8–25 minutes when the verified story supports it; the run request Target duration (180–1200s) overrides this default. NARRATION: Simple English. ASPECT: 16:9 for playback; a separate optional 16:9 promotional thumbnail.

SOURCE FIRST: No invented facts, dialogue, people, countdowns or rescue attempts.

RETENTION FIRST: Clear immediate stakes, consequential progress, useful intermediate payoffs and a complete ending.

SCRIPT STATUS: DRAFT → READY FOR REVIEW → LOCKED only after explicit approval. Production cannot modify the locked script. Estimated timing must be replaced after rendered narration.

📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS
WORKFLOW GUIDE — how to use this file

THE BIBLE — static reference: people, locations, visual style, documentary accuracy, negative prompt, style tags

SCRIPT PROMPT — creative pass: run first

PRODUCTION PROMPT — asset pass: run second

PART 1 — 🧭 WORKFLOW GUIDE
How to Use the Split System
THE THREE WORKING PARTS
THE BIBLE: Stable channel rules plus episode-specific verified people, locations, objects and timeline. Use alongside both passes.

THE SCRIPT PROMPT: Take source-backed content and output Sections 1, 2 and 2B. This is a draft for review, wrapped in <script>...</script>.

THE PRODUCTION PROMPT: Take the explicitly locked script and Bible; output chronologically ordered visual prompts (<image_prompt[N]> and <video_prompt[N]>), overlays and publishing metadata without changing narration.

WORKFLOW PER VIDEO
STEP 1: PREPARE INPUTS
Plaintext
Type: A (Survival / Escape Story) or B (Rescue / Incident Investigation)
Format: LONG — IMAGE + VIDEO [fixed in this template]
Title: [Optional working title]
Target Duration: [12–18 minutes by default; 8–25 minutes when the verified story supports it; the run request Target duration (180–1200s) overrides this default]
Content: [Case summary supported by the supplied evidence]
Sources:
S01 | [Title] | [Author/authority] | [Date] | [URL] | [Relevant page/section]
S02 | [Title] | [Author/authority] | [Date] | [URL] | [Relevant page/section]

[AGAINST THE ODDS EDITORIAL RULES]
These rules update Against the Odds' research, narration, ending and engagement instructions below. Preserve the existing English language, output sections, extraction tags, asset numbering, media modes, visual style, faceless depiction policy, reconstruction disclosures and exact narration-to-scene mapping. Work silently and use the existing evidence/production sections; do not add a new editorial-analysis section.

VERIFY THE STORY BEFORE COMMITTING TO THE HOOK: Establish the documented predicament, actual people, place, chronology, available resources, failed options, decisive action and supported outcome. Tie material claims to identifiable sources in the existing evidence notes; prefer investigation/rescue reports, expedition records and attributed firsthand accounts, with reliable corroboration where available. Separate documented facts, estimates, disputed accounts, attributed recollections and unknowns. An encyclopedia snippet or model recollection alone is not proof of a precise claim. Treat a preselected hook as provisional and revise unsupported promises. If a material gap blocks a factual account, use the template's existing research-required process; never fill it with fiction.

OPEN AT THE VERIFIED PREDICAMENT: Compare three source-supported openings internally: immediate danger, an obvious escape that failed, and a surprising documented constraint. Select the clearest one a new viewer can understand without the title. Start with a short factual sentence naming the person or group and the concrete problem; the first visual must show that same predicament, equipment or geography. The next sentence supplies an actual constraint, action or consequence rather than restarting with biography, a location lecture or a topic introduction. No invented countdown, superlative, quotation, private thought, last breath or rescue uncertainty. Do not imply the outcome is unknown when it is established; suspense can come from how the documented result became possible.

CAUSE AND EFFECT, NOT SENSATIONALISM: Follow danger -> constrained choices -> documented attempts/setbacks -> decisive action or assistance -> verified outcome. Each sentence must add necessary context, a resource constraint, an action, new evidence, a changed option or a consequence. Explain why an option was unavailable only when the sources support that link. Track what survivors and rescuers knew at each point; do not give one group another's information prematurely. Attribute testimony naturally. Use simple spoken English, concrete verbs, clear subjects and emotional breaths. Cut repeated danger descriptions, repeated praise, decorative geography and generic inspirational morals. Do not exaggerate injuries, suffering, weather, distances, durations, casualty counts or the scale of a disaster. Never turn a documented survival action into universal medical or survival advice.

LONG VIDEOS: Use the selected long-form runtime and develop connected factual questions across the existing chapters. Each chapter must explain an attempt, resource change, search difficulty, discovery or consequential decision, answer its immediate question and advance the chronology. Bring in background when it explains the next action; do not restart the introduction or recap the danger at every chapter. Reorder exposition only when it does not misrepresent the actual sequence or what people knew. Give useful intermediate answers and show the decisive action, rescue/assistance and full supported outcome before the close.

EARN THE ENDING: State what actually happened, including uncertainty, fatalities, unresolved missing people or later consequences when relevant and supported. Do not force a triumphant ending or imply willpower alone caused survival. Credit documented help and circumstance. End the story on a concrete consequence or detail whose significance is now clear; no withheld answer, invented next-episode tease or repeated moral. Keep generated visuals identifiable as reconstructions, not archival evidence. Do not invent a real person's face, actions, dialogue or equipment to make the hook more dramatic.

ONE VARIED ENGAGEMENT CLOSE: After the complete outcome, include ONE compact English invitation to like the video, subscribe to Against the Odds and leave ONE case-specific comment. Reserve approximately 8–12 seconds within the selected runtime. This replaces the legacy optional subscribe-only CTA. Use the existing final narration/follow/end-card slots as one close, without repeating the engagement speech or adding silent padding. Keep its tone proportionate to the real event, especially when people died or remain missing.

VARY THE COMMENT INVITATION: Ask one concrete, respectful question about a documented turning point, constraint, resource, rescue contribution or surprising verified detail. Vary the question and sentence structure with the case, rather than always asking 'Would you survive?' or demanding the same slogan. Do not ask viewers to judge a survivor's worth, blame victims, repeat dangerous actions, disclose trauma or compete over suffering. Align the pinned comment with the spoken question; do not pile on extra questions or ask for repeated comments. The verified answer must never depend on likes, comments or subscriptions.

Example patterns to adapt only when the facts support them: 'Which decision made rescue possible? Comment below, and like and subscribe for more Against the Odds stories.' / 'What surprised you most about the search? Tell us below. Like the video and subscribe for more documented stories.' / 'Which mattered more here: the signal or the search? Leave your choice below, and like and subscribe.' Replace broad wording with the actual decision, resource or detail when possible. Do not invent facts to fit an example, use guilt or false rewards, or import devotional slogans or fictional rule-breaking language.

FINAL SILENT CHECK: The hook and its next sentence advance the same verified predicament; important claims have sources; uncertainties remain qualified; chronology and knowledge states are accurate; every beat adds information; the outcome fully answers the opening promise before the CTA. Closing words contain like + subscribe + one varied case-specific comment invitation, within the selected runtime, exactly once in the clean script and matching final CTA narration segment(s). Preserve all original tags, overlay sections and reconstruction safeguards. Do not output these checks or predict audience retention scores.

“The exit was underwater.”

“They survived the crash. Then the cold arrived.”

The hook must be the first spoken line. Never start with “Welcome back,” “Today we will talk about,” the channel name or an episode number. Do not use unsupported superlatives, invented countdowns or false mysteries.
